subject: Math
topic: Arithmetic Progression - Nth Term, Series Summation & Distinct Problem Archetypes

source_provenance.source_title: NCERT Class X Mathematics Chapter 5 & Authentic SSC CGL / CHSL / CDS Exam Compendium

concepts.name: Definition of Arithmetic Progression & Common Difference
concepts.definition: A sequence of numbers in which each term after the first is obtained by adding a constant d (common difference) to the preceding term.
concepts.conditions: d = a_{k+1} - a_k for all k >= 1. Common difference d can be positive, negative, or zero.

concepts.name: General Term (Nth Term) Formula
concepts.definition: The nth term a_n of an AP with first term a and common difference d is given by a_n = a + (n - 1)d.
concepts.conditions: n must be a positive integer (n in N).

concepts.name: Nth Term from the End
concepts.definition: The m-th term from the end of a finite AP with last term l is given by a'_m = l - (m - 1)d.
concepts.conditions: m <= total number of terms n.

concepts.name: Condition for Three Quantities in AP
concepts.definition: Three numbers a, b, c are in AP if and only if 2b = a + c, where b = (a + c)/2 is the Arithmetic Mean of a and c.
concepts.conditions: Symmetrical representation: a - d, a, a + d.

concepts.name: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
concepts.definition: The sum S_n = (n/2)[2a + (n - 1)d] or S_n = (n/2)(a + l), where l is the nth (last) term.
concepts.conditions: If S_n is given as an algebraic quadratic An^2 + Bn, then common difference d = 2A and first term a = A + B.

concepts.name: Arithmetic Means (AM)
concepts.definition: When k numbers A_1, A_2, ..., A_k are inserted between a and b such that a, A_1, ..., A_k, b form an AP, the common difference is D = (b - a)/(k + 1).
concepts.conditions: The sum of all k inserted AMs equals k times the single AM of a and b: Sum = k * (a + b)/2.

problem_patterns.title: Nth Term Forward Calculation & Index Solving
problem_patterns.deep_structure: Linear relationship between term value and integer index n in an AP
problem_patterns.governing_method: Apply a_n = a + (n-1)d, isolate unknown variable, verify integer validity of index n
decision_points: Compute common difference d = a_2 - a_1 noting sign
Formulate linear equation in index n
Assert n is a positive integer
common_traps: Off-by-one error using n instead of (n - 1)
Sign errors when common difference d is negative

problem_patterns.title: Boundary Terms, Term from End & Sign Inversion
problem_patterns.deep_structure: Positional calculation from the terminal end or finding the first negative/positive term boundary
problem_patterns.governing_method: Use a'_m = l - (m-1)d or set inequality a_n < 0 to solve for minimal integer index n
decision_points: Distinguish counting from beginning versus counting from terminal end
Solve inequality a + (n-1)d < 0 and round up to next integer for index
common_traps: Inverting inequality sign incorrectly when dividing by negative common difference
Failing to subtract from last term l when counting from the end

problem_patterns.title: Algebraic Conditions & Symmetrical Term Selections
problem_patterns.deep_structure: Linear equations formed by multi-term constraints or symmetrical choices (a-d, a, a+d)
problem_patterns.governing_method: Apply 2b = a + c for 3 terms, or solve simultaneous equations for unknown a and d
decision_points: Use symmetrical variables (a-d, a, a+d) when sum of terms is known to cancel d
Use (a-3d, a-d, a+d, a+3d) with step 2d for 4 symmetrical terms
common_traps: Assuming step is d instead of 2d when using symmetrical 4-term representation
Algebraic expansion errors in product relations

problem_patterns.title: Series Summation & Quadratic Term Count Determination
problem_patterns.deep_structure: Summation S_n leading to linear or quadratic relations in term count n
problem_patterns.governing_method: Use S_n = (n/2)[2a + (n-1)d], rearrange to an^2 + bn + c = 0, select valid positive integer roots
decision_points: Check whether last term l is known to use S_n = (n/2)(a+l)
Factorize quadratic equation in n and interpret dual positive integer roots
common_traps: Discarding valid second root when terms from first to second root sum to zero
Omission of 1/2 factor in sum formula

problem_patterns.title: Sum Function Decomposition & Ratio of Sums/Terms
problem_patterns.deep_structure: Extracting nth term from sum S_n or transforming ratio of sums to ratio of terms via n -> 2m - 1
problem_patterns.governing_method: Use a_n = S_n - S_{n-1} or substitute n = 2m - 1 into ratio of sums expression
decision_points: Differentiate S_n algebraic form to get common difference d = 2A
Replace dummy index n with 2m - 1 to relate sum ratio to m-th term ratio
common_traps: Directly substituting m instead of 2m - 1 in ratio of sums

problem_patterns.title: Real-World Contexts, Arithmetic Means & Geometric Applications
problem_patterns.deep_structure: Translating physical distributions, installments, or inserted means into formal AP parameters
problem_patterns.governing_method: Model initial quantity as a, uniform increase as d, and total as S_n; apply AM insertion formula
decision_points: Identify whether the asked quantity is a specific installment (a_n) or total amount (S_n)
Calculate step difference D = (b - a)/(k + 1) for k inserted arithmetic means
common_traps: Confusing total sum S_n with a specific term a_n in word problems
Dividing by k instead of (k + 1) for inserted arithmetic means

source_problems.statement: Which term of the arithmetic progression 21, 18, 15, ... is -81?
source_solution_steps: First term a = 21, common difference d = 18 - 21 = -3.

hints.tier1_conceptual: Identify the first term and common step size of the sequence, then express the general term formula for an arbitrary index.
hints.tier2_strategic: Use a_n = a + (n - 1)d and set it equal to the target negative value.
hints.tier3_next_step: Isolate the term (n - 1) by subtracting the initial term and dividing by the negative common difference, then solve for the integer index n.

source_problems.statement: The 11th term of the arithmetic progression -3, -1/2, 2, ... is:
source_solution_steps: First term a = -3, second term a_2 = -1/2.
To find the 11th term: a_11 = a + (11 - 1)d = a + 10d.

hints.tier1_conceptual: Calculate the constant difference between consecutive terms carefully handling fractional subtraction with negative signs.
hints.tier2_strategic: Apply the nth term formula a_n = a + (n - 1)d specifically for index n = 11.
hints.tier3_next_step: Multiply the 10 step intervals by the fractional common difference 5/2 before adding the negative first term.

source_problems.statement: Check whether -150 is a term of the AP: 11, 8, 5, 2, ...
options: No, because n is not a natural number
No, because the sequence does not contain negative numbers
source_problems.correct_answer: No, because n is not a natural number
source_solution_steps: First term a = 11, common difference d = 8 - 11 = -3.
Assume -150 is the nth term: a_n = a + (n - 1)d = -150.
Since the term index n must be a positive integer (natural number), -150 cannot be a term of this AP.

hints.tier1_conceptual: Assume the given value is the nth term and evaluate whether the resulting index satisfies the fundamental constraint of sequence indexing.
hints.tier2_strategic: Set up a + (n - 1)d = -150 with a = 11 and d = -3, and solve for n.
hints.tier3_next_step: Check whether 164 is divisible by 3 without remainder to determine if n is a natural number.

source_problems.statement: Which term of the progression 20, 19(1/4), 18(1/2), 17(3/4), ... is the first negative term?
source_solution_steps: We require the nth term to be strictly less than 0: a_n < 0.
The smallest integer greater than 27.67 is n = 28.
Therefore, the 28th term is the first negative term.

hints.tier1_conceptual: Express the condition for a term being negative as a strict inequality a_n < 0, and find the smallest integer index that satisfies it.
hints.tier2_strategic: Substitute the initial value and the fractional negative common difference into a + (n - 1)d < 0.
hints.tier3_next_step: Isolate n by inverting the inequality when dividing by negative quantities, and select the next immediate integer ceiling.

source_problems.statement: Determine the AP whose 3rd term is 16 and the 7th term exceeds the 5th term by 12.
source_solution_steps: Express in terms of a and d: (a + 6d) - (a + 4d) = 12 => 2d = 12 => d = 6.
Substitute d = 6 into Equation 1: a + 2(6) = 16 => a + 12 = 16 => a = 4.
Thus the sequence is: a = 4, a + d = 10, a + 2d = 16, a + 3d = 22, ...

hints.tier1_conceptual: Translate the two verbal conditions into simultaneous linear equations involving the initial term and the common difference.
hints.tier2_strategic: Notice that the difference between the 7th and 5th terms directly equals 2d, allowing immediate solution for the step size.
hints.tier3_next_step: Substitute the found common difference into the 3rd term equation a + 2d = 16 to solve for the first term a.

source_problems.statement: Find the 20th term from the last term of the AP: 3, 8, 13, ..., 253.
source_solution_steps: The AP is: 3, 8, 13, ..., 253. Common difference d = 8 - 3 = 5.
Formula for the m-th term from the end: a'_m = l - (m - 1)d.
(Alternative approach: Reverse the AP: 253, 248, ..., first term A = 253, D = -5, A_20 = 253 + 19(-5) = 158).

hints.tier1_conceptual: To count from the end of a sequence, subtract multiples of the common difference from the terminal value, or equivalently reverse the sequence.
hints.tier2_strategic: Use the formula a'_m = l - (m - 1)d with terminal term l = 253 and step size d = 5.
hints.tier3_next_step: Compute 19 multiplied by 5 and subtract this total offset from the last term 253.

source_problems.statement: For what value of k will (2k + 1), (4k - 1), and (5k + 1) be three consecutive terms of an AP?
source_solution_steps: Three terms a, b, c are in AP if and only if 2b = a + c (Arithmetic Mean property).
Verification: For k = 4, terms are 2(4)+1=9, 4(4)-1=15, 5(4)+1=21. Sequence 9, 15, 21 is in AP with d = 6.

hints.tier1_conceptual: Recall that in any arithmetic progression, twice the middle term must strictly equal the sum of the adjacent terms.
hints.tier2_strategic: Formulate the linear relation 2 * (middle term) = (first term) + (third term).
hints.tier3_next_step: Expand both sides of 2(4k - 1) = (2k + 1) + (5k + 1) and collect like terms in k to isolate the variable.

source_problems.statement: The sum of three numbers in an AP is 21 and their product is 231. What is the smallest of these three numbers?
source_solution_steps: Represent the three terms symmetrically as (a - d), a, (a + d).
Sum of terms: (a - d) + a + (a + d) = 3a = 21 => a = 7.
Product of terms: (a - d) * a * (a + d) = a(a^2 - d^2) = 231.
In either case, the smallest of the three numbers is 3.

hints.tier1_conceptual: Choose symmetrical variables (a - d, a, a + d) so that adding the terms eliminates the common difference immediately.
hints.tier2_strategic: Solve for the middle term a from the sum, then substitute into the product relation a(a^2 - d^2) = 231.
hints.tier3_next_step: Divide the product by the known middle term 7, subtract from 49 to isolate d^2, and determine the smallest term.

source_problems.statement: The sum of four consecutive numbers in an AP is 32 and the ratio of the product of the first and the last term to the product of the two middle terms is 7 : 15. Find the greatest number.
source_solution_steps: Represent 4 numbers in AP symmetrically as (a - 3d), (a - d), (a + d), (a + 3d) with common step 2d.
Sum of terms: (a - 3d) + (a - d) + (a + d) + (a + 3d) = 4a = 32 => a = 8.
Product of means: (a - d)(a + d) = a^2 - d^2 = 64 - d^2.

hints.tier1_conceptual: For four terms in AP, use the symmetrical representation (a - 3d, a - d, a + d, a + 3d) where the common difference between adjacent terms is 2d.
hints.tier2_strategic: Find a from the sum 4a = 32, then set up the ratio (a^2 - 9d^2) / (a^2 - d^2) = 7/15.
hints.tier3_next_step: Cross-multiply to solve the linear relation in d^2, take the positive square root, and evaluate the maximal term a + 3d.

source_problems.statement: If m times the m-th term of an AP is equal to n times its n-th term (where m != n), then its (m + n)-th term is:
source_solution_steps: Using general term formula: m[a + (m - 1)d] = n[a + (n - 1)d].
Since m != n, we have (m - n) != 0, so: a + (m + n - 1)d = 0.
Notice that a + (m + n - 1)d is precisely the formula for the (m + n)-th term, a_{m+n}.

hints.tier1_conceptual: Substitute the algebraic formula for both terms and collect all terms on one side to factor out the non-zero difference (m - n).
hints.tier2_strategic: Expand m[a + (m - 1)d] - n[a + (n - 1)d] = 0 and group the coefficients of a and d separately.
hints.tier3_next_step: Factorize the quadratic expression (m^2 - n^2) - (m - n) as (m - n)(m + n - 1) to reveal the expression for the (m + n)th term.

source_problems.statement: Find the sum of the first 22 terms of the arithmetic progression 8, 3, -2, ...
source_solution_steps: First term a = 8, common difference d = 3 - 8 = -5, n = 22.

hints.tier1_conceptual: Apply the standard series summation formula using the count of terms, initial value, and common difference.
hints.tier2_strategic: Substitute a = 8, d = -5, and n = 22 into S_n = (n/2)[2a + (n - 1)d].
hints.tier3_next_step: Evaluate the terms inside the square brackets first: 16 minus 105, before multiplying by the factor 11.

source_problems.statement: Find the sum of the first 100 terms of the AP: 0.6, 1.7, 2.8, ...

hints.tier1_conceptual: Carefully track decimal arithmetic when computing the common difference and the cumulative sum.
hints.tier2_strategic: Set up S_100 = (100/2) * [2a + 99d] with initial term 0.6 and step difference 1.1.
hints.tier3_next_step: Compute 99 multiplied by 1.1, add 1.2, and multiply the resulting bracket sum 110.1 by 50.

source_problems.statement: The first and last terms of an AP are 5 and 45 respectively, and the sum of all terms is 400. Find the common difference.
source_solution_steps: Given: first term a = 5, last term l = 45, sum S_n = 400.
Using first and last term sum formula: S_n = (n/2)(a + l).
Now find common difference using last term: a_n = l = a + (n - 1)d.

hints.tier1_conceptual: First determine the total number of terms using the first-and-last term summation formula, then use the terminal term to find the step size.
hints.tier2_strategic: Use S_n = (n/2)(a + l) to solve directly for integer count n.
hints.tier3_next_step: Equate the 16th term formula a + 15d to 45 and reduce the resulting fraction 40/15 to lowest terms.

source_problems.statement: How many terms of the AP: 24, 21, 18, ... must be taken so that their sum is 78?
source_solution_steps: First term a = 24, common difference d = 21 - 24 = -3, sum S_n = 78.

Pedagogical explanation of dual answer: Since common difference is negative, terms after the 4th term become negative and the sum from 5th to 13th term is exactly 0. Hence both n = 4 and n = 13 yield sum 78.

hints.tier1_conceptual: Formulate a quadratic equation in term count n from the sum formula, and interpret why a decreasing AP can have two positive integer solutions.
hints.tier2_strategic: Substitute a = 24, d = -3, and S_n = 78 into S_n = (n/2)[2a + (n - 1)d] and simplify into standard form.
hints.tier3_next_step: Divide through by 3 to get n^2 - 17n + 52 = 0, find two numbers that multiply to 52 and add to -17, and state both integer roots.

source_problems.statement: Find the sum of all two-digit numbers which are divisible by 3.
source_solution_steps: The two-digit numbers divisible by 3 start at 12 and end at 99.
This is an AP with first term a = 12, common difference d = 3, last term l = 99.
Find the number of terms: l = a + (n - 1)d => 99 = 12 + (n - 1)*3.
Calculate the sum using first and last term formula: S_n = (n/2)(a + l).

hints.tier1_conceptual: Identify the smallest and largest numbers within the specified boundary that meet the divisibility criterion to form the boundary terms.
hints.tier2_strategic: Determine the term count n using the nth term formula with a = 12, d = 3, and last term 99.
hints.tier3_next_step: Apply the shortcut sum formula S_n = (n/2)(a + l) multiplying half the term count by 111.

source_problems.statement: If the sum of first n terms of an AP is given by S_n = 3n^2 + 5n and its m-th term is 164, find the value of m.
source_solution_steps: We know that the nth term is given by: a_n = S_n - S_{n-1}.
(Shortcut check: If S_n = An^2 + Bn, common difference is 2A = 2(3) = 6, and a_1 = S_1 = 8, so a_n = 8 + (n-1)6 = 6n + 2).
Given that the m-th term is 164: a_m = 6m + 2 = 164.

hints.tier1_conceptual: Recall that the nth term is the difference between the sum of first n terms and the sum of first (n - 1) terms.
hints.tier2_strategic: Derive the general expression for a_n by evaluating S_n - S_{n-1}, yielding a linear expression in n.
hints.tier3_next_step: Equate the linear expression 6m + 2 to 164, subtract 2, and divide by the coefficient 6.

source_problems.statement: If the sum of first p terms of an AP is equal to the sum of first q terms (where p != q), then what is the sum of its first (p + q) terms?
source_solution_steps: Since p != q, we divide by (p - q): 2a + (p + q - 1)d = 0.
Now, formula for S_{p+q} is: S_{p+q} = ((p + q)/2) * [2a + (p + q - 1)d].

hints.tier1_conceptual: Equate the sum formulas for p and q terms, bring all terms to one side, and factor out (p - q).
hints.tier2_strategic: Observe the resulting factor [2a + (p + q - 1)d] which is precisely the bracketed core of the sum of (p + q) terms.
hints.tier3_next_step: Since the inner bracket evaluates to zero, multiply by (p + q)/2 to establish the total sum.

source_problems.statement: The ratio of the sums of m and n terms of an AP is m^2 : n^2. Show or find the ratio of their m-th and n-th terms.
source_solution_steps: 2a(n - m) = [m(n - 1) - n(m - 1)]d = [mn - m - mn + n]d = (n - m)d.
Since m != n, divide by (n - m): 2a = d, or d = 2a.
Now, ratio of m-th to n-th term: a_m / a_n = [a + (m - 1)d] / [a + (n - 1)d].

hints.tier1_conceptual: Cancel the common factors m and n from the sum ratio to relate the bracketed expressions [2a + (m - 1)d] and [2a + (n - 1)d].
hints.tier2_strategic: Solve the cross-multiplication to express the common difference d directly in terms of the initial term a.
hints.tier3_next_step: Substitute d = 2a into the ratio of general terms [a + (m - 1)d] / [a + (n - 1)d] and simplify the linear coefficients.

source_problems.statement: Find the middle term of the arithmetic progression 6, 13, 20, ..., 216.
source_solution_steps: First term a = 6, common difference d = 13 - 6 = 7, last term l = 216.
Find the total number of terms n: a_n = a + (n - 1)d = 216.
Since n = 31 is odd, there is exactly one middle term at position (n + 1)/2 = (31 + 1)/2 = 16th term.
Calculate the 16th term: a_16 = a + (16 - 1)d = a + 15d.
(Shortcut check: Middle term = (First term + Last term)/2 = (6 + 216)/2 = 222/2 = 111).

hints.tier1_conceptual: Determine the total count of terms first, then find the central index for an odd number of terms.
hints.tier2_strategic: Solve 6 + 7(n - 1) = 216 to find total terms n = 31, and identify index (31 + 1)/2.
hints.tier3_next_step: Alternatively, use the symmetry property that the middle term of an odd-length AP equals the average of the first and last terms (6 + 216)/2.

source_problems.statement: In an AP of 24 terms, if a_1 + a_5 + a_10 + a_15 + a_20 + a_24 = 225, find the sum of all 24 terms.
source_solution_steps: Fundamental AP symmetry theorem: The sum of terms equidistant from the beginning and the end is constant and equal to (a_1 + a_n).
Notice the equidistant pairs among the 6 given terms in a 24-term AP:
Now, formula for the sum of all 24 terms is: S_24 = (24 / 2) * (a_1 + a_24).

hints.tier1_conceptual: Group the given terms into pairs that are equidistant from the beginning and end of the 24-term sequence.
hints.tier2_strategic: Observe that each of the three pairs (1, 24), (5, 20), and (10, 15) sums to identical value (2a + 23d).
hints.tier3_next_step: Divide 225 by 3 to get the sum of first and last terms (a_1 + a_24), then multiply by 12 (half of 24) to find S_24.

source_problems.statement: If n arithmetic means are inserted between 3 and 17 such that the ratio of the first mean to the last mean is 1 : 3, what is the value of n?
source_solution_steps: Let the n arithmetic means inserted between 3 and 17 be A_1, A_2, ..., A_n.
The complete sequence is: 3, A_1, A_2, ..., A_n, 17 with total (n + 2) terms.

hints.tier1_conceptual: Recall that when n means are inserted between a and b, the common difference is D = (b - a)/(n + 1).
hints.tier2_strategic: Express the first mean as a + D and the last mean as b - D in terms of n, and form their ratio.
hints.tier3_next_step: Cross-multiply 3(3n + 17) = 17n + 3, subtract 9n from 17n, and divide 48 by 8 to obtain integer n.

source_problems.statement: If 10 arithmetic means are inserted between 7 and 73, what is the sum of these 10 arithmetic means?
source_solution_steps: Theorem: The sum of n arithmetic means inserted between two quantities a and b is always equal to n times the single arithmetic mean of a and b.
Formula: Sum of means = n * ((a + b) / 2).

hints.tier1_conceptual: Use the master property that the sum of all inserted arithmetic means equals the number of means multiplied by the average of the boundary endpoints.
hints.tier2_strategic: Calculate the arithmetic mean of the two boundaries (7 + 73)/2.
hints.tier3_next_step: Multiply the calculated average 40 by the count of inserted means 10 to obtain the total sum directly.

source_problems.statement: A manufacturer of TV sets produced 600 sets in the third year and 700 sets in the seventh year. Assuming that the production increases uniformly by a fixed number every year, find the total production in the first 7 years.
source_solution_steps: Let production in 1st year be a, and annual uniform increase be d.
Now find total production in first 7 years (S_7):

hints.tier1_conceptual: Translate the 3rd and 7th year production figures into linear expressions a + 2d and a + 6d.
hints.tier2_strategic: Solve for uniform annual increase d by subtracting the equations, then find initial output a.
hints.tier3_next_step: Compute the total 7-year sum using S_7 = (7/2)[2a + 6d] by multiplying 7 by half of 1250.

source_problems.statement: A person agrees to pay off a loan of Rs. 1,18,000 by paying every month. In the first month he pays Rs. 1,000 and then increases the payment by Rs. 100 every month. What amount will he pay in the 30th installment?
source_solution_steps: The installment payments form an AP: 1000, 1100, 1200, ...
We need to find the specific payment made in the 30th installment, which is the 30th term a_30.
Therefore, the amount paid in the 30th installment is Rs. 3,900.

hints.tier1_conceptual: Distinguish between finding an individual monthly payment (a single term a_n) versus the cumulative loan repayment (a sum S_n).
hints.tier2_strategic: Set up the nth term formula a_30 = a + 29d with starting payment 1000 and increment 100.
hints.tier3_next_step: Multiply 29 by 100 and add the initial payment of 1000 to determine the 30th payment.

source_problems.statement: The angles of a quadrilateral are in arithmetic progression whose common difference is 10 degrees. What is the measure of the smallest angle?
source_solution_steps: Let the four angles in AP be a, a + d, a + 2d, a + 3d.
Angles are: a, a + 10, a + 20, a + 30.
The sum of all interior angles of a quadrilateral is strictly 360 degrees.
Therefore, the smallest angle is 75 degrees.

hints.tier1_conceptual: Combine the geometric theorem that the sum of angles of a quadrilateral is 360 degrees with the AP term formulation.
hints.tier2_strategic: Express the four angles as a, a + 10, a + 20, a + 30 and sum them to 360.
hints.tier3_next_step: Subtract the sum of constant angle steps 60 from 360 and divide the remainder 300 by 4.

source_problems.statement: In a potato race, a bucket is placed at the starting point, which is 5 m from the first potato, and the other potatoes are placed 3 m apart in a straight line. There are 10 potatoes in the line. A competitor starts from the bucket, picks up the nearest potato, runs back with it, drops it in the bucket, runs back to pick up the next potato, and continues until all potatoes are in the bucket. What is the total distance the competitor has to run?
source_solution_steps: Distance to pick up and return the 1st potato: 2 * 5 = 10 m.
The round-trip distances form an AP: 10, 16, 22, ... for 10 potatoes.
First term a = 10, common difference d = 16 - 10 = 6, number of terms n = 10.
Total distance run is the sum S_10:

hints.tier1_conceptual: Remember to double each one-way distance to account for running to the potato and returning to the bucket.
hints.tier2_strategic: Recognize that the round-trip distances form an AP starting at 10 with a common step size of 6.
hints.tier3_next_step: Compute S_10 using the sum formula with n = 10, a = 10, and d = 6, multiplying 5 by the bracketed sum 74.
